mainTopic: Which kinds of kneading (גלגול) exempt dough from חלה: kneading while the dough is הקדש, and kneading while it belongs to a גוי
overview: The גמרא carries the rules about smoothing grain (מירוח) over to kneading dough (גלגול) for חלה. A משנה proves that dough kneaded while it was הקדש stays exempt from חלה even after it is redeemed. רבא then asks about dough kneaded while a גוי owned it, and a משנה about a גר shows that it is exempt. The גמרא asks whose view that משנה follows. It might be everyone's, because only the מעשרות verses have an extra ״דגנך״. Or it might be only רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון, since רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה could learn חלה from מעשרות through ״ראשית״ ״ראשית״. רבא wishes to see the answer in a dream, and then rules that גלגול גוי follows מירוח גוי for each opinion. רב פפא and רבינא challenge him from ברייתות that obligate a גוי's תרומה but exempt his חלה. The גמרא answers that the obligation on the גוי's grain there is only מדרבנן, a גזירה because of wealthy people.

steps.title: Kneading while consecrated exempts dough from חלה
steps.stepSummary: A rule is stated: if dough was kneaded while it was הקדש, it is exempt from חלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Kneading of consecrated dough exempts it from חלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states a new rule about חלה: dough kneaded while it belonged to הקדש is exempt. Proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the גמרא said that smoothing grain (מירוח) while it was הקדש exempts it from מעשרות. This rule is the same idea for חלה. For dough, the moment of obligation is the kneading (גלגול).

keyTerms.meaning: Kneading or rolling the dough. This is the moment the חלה obligation starts.
Property that belongs to the בית המקדש
Exempts

phrases.english: Kneading of consecrated dough exempts it,
phrases.notes: This is רבא adding to the earlier rule about grain smoothed while it was הקדש. It exempts the dough from חלה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries the earlier מירוח הקדש rule for מעשרות over to חלה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dough kneaded while it was הקדש is exempt from חלה, even after it is redeemed.

steps.title: Proof from a משנה about consecrated dough
steps.stepSummary: A משנה in חלה lists three cases. Only dough kneaded by the Temple treasurer while it was הקדש is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: if she consecrated her dough before kneading it and then redeemed it, she is obligated. If she consecrated it after kneading and then redeemed it, she is obligated. If she consecrated it before kneading, the treasurer kneaded it, and afterward she redeemed it, she is exempt, because at the time it became obligated it was exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to prove the rule from step 1. Dough kneaded while it was הקדש stays exempt from חלה, even after it is redeemed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everything depends on who owned the dough at the moment of kneading. In the first two cases she owned it at that moment, so she is obligated. In the third case it belonged to הקדש when the גזבר kneaded it, so the obligation never started.

keyTerms.meaning: She consecrated it to the בית המקדש
She redeemed it, buying it back from הקדש
The Temple treasurer
The moment its obligation starts, which is the kneading
Obligated / exempt

steps.whatToRemember: For חלה, what matters is who owns the dough at the moment of kneading. If it was הקדש then, it is exempt forever.

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן: הִקְדִּישָׁהּ עִיסָּתָהּ עַד שֶׁלֹּא גִּלְגְּלָה
phrases.english: As we learned: If she consecrated her dough before she kneaded it
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in מסכת חלה.

phrases.english: and she redeemed it, she is obligated;
if she consecrated it after she kneaded it and redeemed it, she is obligated;
if she consecrated it before she kneaded it,
and the treasurer kneaded it,
and afterward she redeemed it, she is exempt,
for at the time of its obligation it was exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: הִקְדִּישָׁהּ עִיסָּתָהּ עַד שֶׁלֹּא גִּלְגְּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the rule in step 1
steps.raayaObject: The rule that kneading while the dough is הקדש exempts it from חלה
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה חלה 3:3, the case where the גזבר kneaded consecrated dough

steps.title: רבא asks about dough kneaded by a גוי
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks what the law is if the dough was kneaded while a גוי owned it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: What is the law of kneading by a gentile?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know kneading by הקדש exempts, רבא asks whether kneading while a גוי owns the dough also exempts it from חלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, smoothing grain while a גוי owned it was disputed: רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה obligate, while others exempt. רבא wants to know how this works for kneading dough. He is asking about a Jew who gets the dough after it was kneaded.

keyTerms.meaning: Kneading done while a gentile owns the dough
What is the law?

phrases.english: Rava asked: Kneading by a gentile, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from kneading by הקדש to kneading by a גוי
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does kneading while a גוי owns the dough exempt it from חלה?

steps.title: A משנה about a גר answers the question
steps.stepSummary: A משנה rules that a גר's dough made before he converted is exempt, dough made after is obligated, and in a doubt it is obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is taught in a משנה: A convert who converted and had dough. If it was made before he converted, he is exempt. If after he converted, he is obligated. If it is a doubt, he is obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבא from an explicit משנה. Dough kneaded while its owner was still a גוי is exempt from חלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גר whose dough was made before his conversion owned it as a גוי when it was kneaded. The משנה exempts him, so kneading by a גוי exempts the dough. In a case of doubt he must separate חלה.

keyTerms.meaning: A convert to Judaism
He converted
A doubt, here not knowing whether the dough was made before or after he converted

steps.confusionAlert: The question was about a גוי, but the משנה talks about a גר. It still answers the question, because before he converted, the גר was a גוי who owned the dough.

phrases.english: It is taught explicitly, as we learned:
A convert who converted and had dough,
if it was made before he converted, he is exempt;
if after he converted, he is obligated;
if uncertain, he is obligated.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיתְנָא תְּנַן: גֵּר שֶׁנִּתְגַּיֵּיר וְהָיְתָה לוֹ עִיסָּה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Kneading while a גוי owns the dough exempts it from חלה, as the משנה about a גר shows.

steps.title: Whose opinion is this משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא wrote the משנה about the גר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whose opinion the גר משנה follows. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For grain smoothed by a גוי, רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה obligate and others exempt. The גמרא wants to know if this משנה follows only the side that exempts, or everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא that teaches this?

phrases.english: Who teaches this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks at the משנה just brought and asks whose view it represents
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the גר משנה follow only the opinion that exempts מירוח גוי, or does everyone agree with it?

steps.title: First possibility: everyone agrees, even רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is everyone's opinion. Even רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה, who obligate מירוח גוי for מעשרות, exempt גלגול גוי for חלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is everyone's opinion. Even רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה, who obligate there, exempt here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a first possible answer: maybe everyone agrees with the משנה, even רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה. A second possibility comes in step 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה obligate grain smoothed by a גוי in מעשרות. On this possibility, they would still agree that dough kneaded by a גוי is exempt from חלה. Steps 7–9 explain why they might treat the two differently.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone's opinion, with no dispute
Who obligate
There, by מעשרות / here, by חלה

phrases.english: It is the opinion of everyone,
and even Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda,
who obligate there,
phrases.notes: "There" means grain smoothed by a גוי, for מעשרות.

phrases.english: exempt here.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל הִיא, וַאֲפִילּוּ רַבִּי מֵאִיר וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of whose opinion the משנה is
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Possibly everyone agrees, even רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה, that kneading by a גוי exempts dough from חלה. Step 10 raises the other possibility.

steps.title: Why מעשרות is different: the extra ״דגנך״
steps.stepSummary: By מעשרות, רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה obligate because of an extra word ״דגנך״ in the פסוק. No such extra word exists for חלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is because it is written ״your grain,″ and ״your grain″ again, an extra one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה obligate by מעשרות but not by חלה. By מעשרות the תורה repeats the word ״דגנך״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ״דגנך״ ("your grain") leaves out grain smoothed while it was הקדש. The extra ״דגנך״ teaches that grain smoothed by a גוי is still obligated. חלה has no extra word like this, so the basic rule applies: dough kneaded by a גוי is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: Your grain
Extra, an additional word that teaches something

steps.whatToRemember: According to this first approach, everyone exempts dough kneaded by a גוי from חלה. רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה would obligate מירוח גוי only by מעשרות, because of the extra ״דגנך״. Step 10 offers a different possibility, and in step 12 רבא rules along those other lines.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the same opinion can give different rulings for מעשרות and חלה. The difference comes from the wording of each פסוק.

phrases.english: There it is because it is written: "your grain,"
"your grain" is extra.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the claim in step 6 that רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה treat חלה differently from מעשרות
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the two cases based on the wording of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה obligate מירוח גוי for מעשרות, they should also obligate גלגול גוי for חלה.
steps.terutzMaskana: On this approach, their ruling by מעשרות comes from an extra ״דגנך״ that exists only there. So by חלה, kneading by a גוי would exempt according to everyone.

steps.title: Two restrictions in a row include even a גוי
steps.stepSummary: The extra words in the מעשרות verses make a 'restriction after a restriction', and that rule comes to include, so even a גוי's grain is obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a restriction after a restriction, and a restriction after a restriction only comes to include, even a גוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining the extra word from step 7. It shows how that extra word makes a גוי's grain obligated in מעשרות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule for reading פסוקים: one limiting word excludes, but two limiting words in a row actually include. So according to רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה, the extra 'דגנך' turns the meaning around, and even grain smoothed by a גוי is obligated in מעשרות.

keyTerms.meaning: A limiting word in a פסוק that excludes something
Two limiting words in a row
To include

steps.confusionAlert: It sounds backwards, but two 'limiting' words together do not limit twice as much. The rule is that they come to INCLUDE.

phrases.english: It is a restriction after a restriction,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין מִיעוּט אַחַר מִיעוּט אֶלָּא לְרַבּוֹת,
phrases.english: and a restriction after a restriction comes only to include,
even a gentile.
phrases.notes: He means even grain that was smoothed while a גוי owned it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation of the extra word 'דגנך' given in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual derivation: a hermeneutic rule explains the obligation for מעשרות.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה obligate מירוח גוי, maybe they should also obligate גלגול גוי.
steps.terutzMaskana: Their obligation by מעשרות comes from a special 'restriction after a restriction' in those verses.

steps.title: By חלה, both mentions of 'your dough' are already used
steps.stepSummary: 'עריסותיכם' appears only twice. One teaches the minimum amount, and the other excludes the dough of גוים and of הקדש, so nothing is left over to include a גוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here, 'your dough' is written twice. One 'your dough' teaches the amount of your dough, and one 'your dough' teaches: not the dough of גוים and not the dough of הקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows why the reasoning from מעשרות does not carry over to חלה. The חלה verses have no extra word that could include a גוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of the two words 'עריסותיכם' already has its own job, so there is no 'restriction after a restriction' here. The second one actually excludes a גוי's dough. This is why even רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה exempt גלגול גוי, so the משנה of the גר can fit everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Your dough', the word in the פסוק of חלה
The amount of your dough, which sets the minimum size for חלה
Property dedicated to the בית המקדש

steps.whatToRemember: According to this approach, everyone exempts dough kneaded by a גוי. Even those who obligate מירוח גוי by מעשרות agree, because only the מעשרות verses have the extra word.

phrases.english: But here,
"your dough" is written twice,
one "your dough" teaches the amount of your dough,
phrases.notes: This is the amount of dough they made in the מדבר, an עומר's worth.

phrases.english: and one "your dough" teaches:

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא עִיסַּת גּוֹיִם וְלֹא עִיסַּת הֶקְדֵּשׁ.
phrases.english: and not the dough of gentiles, and not the dough of consecrated property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts the חלה verses with the מעשרות verses explained in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: different verses lead to different results.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: חלה should follow מעשרות, so רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה would obligate גלגול גוי.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both mentions of 'עריסותיכם' are used up, and one of them excludes a גוי. So everyone exempts.

steps.title: Or maybe the משנה follows only רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: A second possibility: the משנה exempting the גר's dough follows רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון. רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה would learn חלה from מעשרות through 'ראשית' and 'ראשית', and so they would obligate.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון taught it, since they exempt. But רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה learn 'ראשית' 'ראשית' from there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a different answer to the question from step 5 (which תנא wrote the משנה?). Maybe the משנה is not everyone's opinion after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון exempt מירוח גוי, so they would also exempt גלגול גוי, and the משנה fits them. רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה might link חלה ('ראשית עריסותיכם') to מעשרות ('ראשית דגנך') through a גזירה שוה. Then their obligation for מעשרות would carry over to חלה.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps, which introduces another possibility
They learn (one law from another)
'First', a word used both by חלה and by מעשרות
Learning one law from another because the same word appears in both

steps.whyThisMatters: This means רבא's question might not have one answer for everyone. Whether גלגול גוי obligates might depend on the מחלוקת about מירוח גוי. רבא decides this in step 12.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן קָתָנֵי לַהּ,
phrases.english: Or perhaps Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Shimon taught it,
phrases.notes: 'It' means the משנה about the גר's dough.

phrases.english: since they exempt,
phrases.notes: They exempt grain smoothed by a גוי from מעשרות, and so also dough kneaded by a גוי.

phrases.english: but Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda
derive "first" "first" from there.
phrases.notes: חלה says 'ראשית עריסותיכם' (במדבר 15:20), and מעשרות says 'ראשית דגנך' (דברים 18:4).

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ דִלְמָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן קָתָנֵי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative to steps 6–9, which said the משנה follows everyone.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא wrote the משנה about the גר (from step 5).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Possibly only רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון. רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה would obligate through the גזירה שוה of 'ראשית'.

steps.title: רבא wishes to see the answer in a dream
steps.stepSummary: Both readings seem possible, so רבא prays to be shown the answer in a dream.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: May it be God's will that I see it in a dream.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא admits that the two approaches are evenly balanced and the question is still open. This sets up his own resolution in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is proven here. This line shows that the גמרא could not decide between step 6 (everyone exempts) and step 10 (it depends on the מחלוקת).

keyTerms.meaning: May it be (God's) will
In a dream

phrases.english: Rava said:
May it be His will that I see it in a dream.
phrases.notes: 'It' means the answer, which of the two approaches is correct.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to the two competing answers in steps 6–10 by leaving them undecided.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling; רבא shows that the question is unresolved.

steps.title: רבא: גלגול follows מירוח
steps.stepSummary: רבא decides that the law of dough kneaded by a גוי follows the law of grain smoothed by a גוי, for both sides of the מחלוקת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then רבא said: Whoever says מירוח by a גוי exempts holds that גלגול by a גוי exempts. Whoever says מירוח by a גוי does not exempt holds that גלגול by a גוי does not exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא resolves his own question from step 3. Dough kneaded by a גוי is treated exactly like grain smoothed by a גוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the second approach (step 10): חלה and מעשרות go together. So there is no single answer for everyone; it depends on which side of the מירוח גוי מחלוקת you follow.

keyTerms.meaning: Smoothing the grain pile, the stage that makes grain obligated in מעשרות
Kneading the dough, the stage that makes dough obligated in חלה
Exempts

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's conclusion: גלגול גוי follows מירוח גוי. If you exempt one, you exempt the other, and if you obligate one, you obligate the other.

phrases.english: Rava then said:
The one who says that smoothing by a gentile exempts —
holds that kneading by a gentile exempts;

phrases.aramaic: מַאן דְּאָמַר מֵירוּחַ הַגּוֹי אֵינוֹ פּוֹטֵר –
phrases.english: the one who says that smoothing by a gentile does not exempt —
holds that kneading by a gentile does not exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא answers the question he left open in step 11.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The law of dough kneaded by a גוי follows the same מחלוקת as grain smoothed by a גוי.

steps.title: רב פפא quotes a ברייתא about a גוי's firstborn donkey and חלה
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא brings a ברייתא: if a גוי separates a lamb for a פטר חמור or separates חלה, we tell him he is exempt. His חלה may be eaten by non-כהנים, and the lamb has no holiness.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא challenged רבא from a ברייתא: A גוי who set aside a lamb for a firstborn donkey, or set aside חלה, is told that he is exempt. His חלה may be eaten by people who are not כהנים, and he may shear and work the lamb.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge against רבא by quoting a ברייתא. The real attack comes in the next step, from what this ברייתא leaves out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says a גוי is not bound by the מצוה of חלה, so his dough is exempt. Notice that it names only פטר חמור and חלה. It does not list תרומה, and the next step builds on that silence.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn donkey, which a Jew must redeem with a lamb
The portion of dough given to a כהן
Non-כהנים
We let him know he is exempt

phrases.english: Rav Pappa raised an objection to Rava:
A gentile who separated [a lamb for] a firstborn donkey, or separated challah,
phrases.notes: For a firstborn donkey, he set aside a lamb to redeem it, the way a Jew would.

phrases.english: we inform him that he is exempt,
and his challah may be eaten by non-priests,
and the firstborn donkey's [lamb], he may shear it and work with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to test רבא's conclusion in Step 12
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule that kneading by a גוי follows smoothing by a גוי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sets up a ברייתא that exempts a גוי's חלה but, as the next step shows, does not exempt his תרומה

steps.title: רב פפא's point: here is a תנא who splits the two cases
steps.stepSummary: From the ברייתא's silence we learn that a גוי's תרומה is real. So this תנא holds that smoothing by a גוי does not exempt, yet kneading by a גוי does exempt. That goes against רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies that his תרומה is forbidden to non-כהנים. So here is a תנא who says smoothing by a גוי does not exempt, but kneading by a גוי does exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא draws an inference from the ברייתא and uses it to attack רבא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists only חלה and פטר חמור as exempt, so a גוי's תרומה must still count as real תרומה. That means this תנא treats grain smoothed by a גוי as obligated. Yet the same תנא treats dough kneaded by a גוי as exempt. רבא said the two always go together, so this is a direct challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce given to a כהן, forbidden to non-כהנים
Smoothing the grain pile, the step that makes grain obligated in מעשרות
Kneading or rolling the dough, the step that makes dough obligated in חלה
"This implies", which introduces an inference from the text

steps.confusionAlert: פּוֹטֵר here means "makes it exempt." So מירוח הגוי אינו פוטר means the grain is still obligated even though a גוי smoothed it, while גלגול גוי פוטר means the dough is exempt.

phrases.english: This implies: his terumah is forbidden [to non-priests],
and here is this tanna who says:
smoothing by a gentile does not exempt,
and kneading by a gentile does exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא תְּרוּמָתוֹ אֲסוּרָה, וְהָא הַאי תַּנָּא דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the ברייתא quoted in Step 13 and aims it at רבא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A תנא who obligates grain smoothed by a גוי yet exempts dough kneaded by a גוי shows that the two laws do not always go together

steps.title: רבינא brings a second ברייתא about חלה in the Land and תרומה outside it
steps.stepSummary: רבינא quotes a ברייתא: a גוי's חלה in ארץ ישראל and his תרומה outside ארץ ישראל are both exempt. This implies that his תרומה in ארץ ישראל is real and forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא also challenged רבא: A גוי's חלה in ארץ ישראל, and his תרומה outside ארץ ישראל, we tell him he is exempt. His חלה may be eaten by non-כהנים, and his תרומה does not make a mixture forbidden. This implies that his תרומה in ארץ ישראל is forbidden and does make a mixture forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא brings another ברייתא against רבא. This one talks about תרומה directly, so the inference is even clearer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the ברייתא exempts a גוי's חלה even inside ארץ ישראל. For תרומה, it exempts only what grows outside ארץ ישראל. So his תרומה inside the Land is real: forbidden to non-כהנים, and it makes a mixture forbidden. Again, grain smoothed by a גוי is obligated while dough kneaded by a גוי is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: In ארץ ישראל
Outside ארץ ישראל
Makes a mixture forbidden; real תרומה mixed into ordinary food forbids the mix to non-כהנים

phrases.english: And Ravina further raised an objection to Rava:
The challah of a gentile in the Land [of Israel],
and his terumah outside the Land —
we inform him that he is exempt,
his challah may be eaten by non-priests,
and his terumah does not make a mixture forbidden.
This implies: his terumah in the Land —
is forbidden and does make a mixture forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, more explicit ברייתא against רבא, alongside רב פפא's challenge
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This ברייתא names תרומה directly, so the inference that a גוי's תרומה in ארץ ישראל is real is explicit

steps.title: רבינא's point: again a תנא splits smoothing and kneading
steps.stepSummary: רבינא concludes that this ברייתא, too, follows a תנא who obligates grain smoothed by a גוי but exempts dough kneaded by a גוי, which goes against רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And here is a תנא who says smoothing by a גוי does not exempt, yet kneading by a גוי does exempt!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא finishes his challenge and spells out how this ברייתא contradicts רבא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This repeats the wording of רב פפא's point, which shows that both ברייתות lead to the same problem. The next step answers both challenges.

keyTerms.meaning: This תנא, the author of the ברייתא
Does not exempt, so the produce stays obligated

steps.whatToRemember: Both רב פפא and רבינא find a תנא who treats a גוי's grain as obligated in תרומה but a גוי's dough as exempt from חלה. That directly challenges רבא's rule that the two always go together.

phrases.english: And here is this tanna who says:
smoothing by a gentile does not exempt,
kneading by a gentile does exempt!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא הַאי תַּנָּא דְּאָמַר: מֵירוּחַ הַגּוֹי אֵינוֹ פּוֹטֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out how the ברייתא in Step 15 contradicts רבא, using the same wording as Step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's conclusion that kneading by a גוי follows smoothing by a גוי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A תנא who obligates the גוי's תרומה in ארץ ישראל but exempts his חלה even in ארץ ישראל treats the two cases differently

steps.title: The grain obligation is only rabbinic, a decree because of wealthy people
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתות that treat a גוי's smoothed grain as obligated in תרומה are speaking only מדרבנן. By Torah law it is exempt. The חכמים made a גזירה because of wealthy people who might try to dodge their obligations.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is only a rabbinic law, a decree because of wealthy people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the questions from רב פפא and רבינא. When those ברייתות treat a גוי's smoothed grain as needing תרומה, that is only a rabbinic rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge was that one תנא seemed to split the two cases: smoothing by a גוי does not exempt, but kneading by a גוי does. The answer is that by Torah law both cases match, since a גוי's action exempts in both. The extra obligation on grain is just a rabbinic גזירה, so the ברייתות do not go against רבא's rule that the two cases follow each other.

keyTerms.meaning: By rabbinic law, not by Torah law
A protective decree the חכמים made to prevent a problem
Wealthy people (literally 'owners of pockets')
Smoothing the grain pile, the step that creates the obligation of תרומה and מעשרות
By Torah law

steps.whatToRemember: According to the תנא of these ברייתות, by Torah law a גוי's smoothing exempts grain, just as a גוי's kneading exempts dough. So the two cases match, as רבא said. The requirement of תרומה from a גוי's smoothed grain is only a rabbinic גזירה, made because of wealthy people.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not conclude from the ברייתות that a גוי's smoothing obligates grain by Torah law. The obligation is only מדרבנן. That is exactly why it does not contradict the exemption for a גוי's kneading.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer saves רבא's rule that the law of kneading follows the law of smoothing. It also shows a common move in the גמרא: an apparent difference between two cases can come from a rabbinic decree, while the Torah-level law stays the same.

phrases.english: It is only by rabbinic law,
phrases.notes: He means the ברייתא's rule that a גוי's smoothed grain still needs תרומה. By Torah law, that grain would be exempt.

phrases.english: a decree because of people of means.
phrases.notes: The worry is that rich owners might put their grain in a גוי's name while it is smoothed, just to get out of giving תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenges of רב פפא and רבינא (steps 14 and 16) against רבא's ruling in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing levels of law: the apparent difference comes from a rabbinic decree, not from Torah law.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתות seemed to hold that a גוי's smoothing does not exempt grain by Torah law, while a גוי's kneading does exempt dough. That would split the two cases and go against רבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: By Torah law, a גוי's smoothing exempts, just like his kneading. The grain obligation in the ברייתות is only a rabbinic גזירה because of wealthy people, so רבא's comparison stands.
